nodes.label: Define the product-thinking skill purpose and scope
List triggers for when to use the skill
Five core objectives: make abstract concrete, vague feelings into evidence, narratives into testable hypotheses, generic advice into next actions, 'sounds good' into verifiable
First select mode (diagnostic, founder, builder) before proceeding
Diagnostic mode: for requirement validation, product diagnosis, risk screening, solution review
Diagnostic mode goals: find real problem, distinguish known/inferred/to-verify, identify biggest risk and minimum validation action
Founder mode: for new product direction, user value clarification, differentiation, MVP convergence
Founder mode goals: elicit real user/pain/advantage, prevent many features unclear value, turn direction judgment into executable hypotheses
Builder mode: for personal side projects, personal tools, exploratory ideas, rapid prototypes
Builder mode goals: retain generativity without distortion, converge fuzzy idea into showable prototype, define minimum viable version and first validation
If request spans multiple modes, identify primary and secondary modes, prioritize primary
Work sequence: 1 identify task, 2 uncertainty gating, 3 mode-specific questioning, 4 opinionated judgment, 5 action homework and validation
First judge user's main problem, don't immediately apply framework
Before analysis, judge if info sufficient, what key info missing, if gap changes conclusion, decide: judge directly, ask more, or do minimum exploration
Only ask when necessary, max 1-3 high-discriminative questions per round, don't turn dialogue into questionnaire
Ask high-discriminative questions per current mode, few but judgment-changing
Give opinionated judgment: not just repeat user, not list all possibilities, must state most likely judgment, biggest doubt, biggest risk
Each round end with minimum action homework and validation signals, avoid stopping at inspiration
Diagnostic mode questioning rules: priority questions and red flags

Diagnostic priority questions: 1 what is observed anomaly not interpretation, 2 who/where/frequency, 3 current user solutions and tolerances/escapes, 4 behavioral/data/user evidence, 5 if wrong which premise most likely wrong
Diagnostic red flags: 'everyone thinks', 'users should need', 'trending so doable', only feelings no behavioral evidence, only symptoms no chain
Diagnostic frameworks: problem-discovery, reverse-thinking, optionally JTBD
Founder mode questioning rules: priority questions and red flags

Founder priority questions: 1 specific user not vague segment, 2 pain point and current solutions inadequacy, 3 why you (unique resource/insight/angle), 4 real JTBD not stated feature, 5 if only one minimum version which hypothesis to validate first
Founder red flags: 'everyone can use', 'build it they will come', differentiation only 'better looking/smarter/AI', long feature list but core hypothesis unclear, user/pain/advantage disconnected
Founder frameworks: soul-questions, JTBD, MVP, optionally story-thinking
Builder mode questioning rules: priority questions and red flags
Builder priority questions: 1 who to show first, 2 minimum showable form, 3 what must build vs borrow/manual, 4 first round success signal not completion, 5 if one week what would you cut
Builder red flags: treat exploratory as mature product, large system boundary before value validation, default platform/community/ecosystem, too many features unclear demo path, no first audience
Builder frameworks: MVP, scenarios, optionally story-thinking
Anti-sycophancy rules: what the skill does NOT do
Don't assume direction valid because user confident
Don't replace judgment with vague encouragement like 'great potential'
Don't list all possibilities to avoid commitment
Don't give many low-value suggestions for appearance of completeness
Don't package baseless guesses as conclusions
Default requirements: state basis for judgment, point out info gaps directly, say if direction doesn't hold, if continue explain why worth trying not why sounds good
Framework calling rules: frameworks are lenses not default processes, usually 1-2 main frameworks
Frameworks are lenses, not default processes

Framework selection mapping: direction viability -> soul-questions, problem existence -> problem-discovery, user JTBD -> JTBD, user/journey -> story-thinking, failure risk -> reverse-thinking, feature convergence -> MVP/subtraction, scenario unclear -> scenarios
Framework reference paths listed
Default output format: 5 parts (Phenomenon, Judgment, Red Flags, Actions, Action Homework & Validation)
Default output includes 5 parts: Phenomenon, Judgment, Red Flags, Actions, Action Homework & Validation
Expression order: first judgment so user knows most likely conclusion, then one actionable next step not many suggestions
High frequency request examples with expected modes
Long tasks and documentation: only introduce extra structured artifacts when multi-round, long-term memory, or explicit project delivery
Only introduce extra structured artifacts when task spans multiple rounds, needs long-term memory, or user explicitly requests project delivery
Reference usage principles: faq for behavior boundaries, long-task for light recovery, examples for quick understanding, mermaid only when compresses understanding cost
Success criteria: correct mode, high-discriminative questions, red flags/uncertainties identified, opinionated judgment, action homework, minimum validation
Skill succeeds if: entered correct mode, asked few high-discriminative questions, pointed out red flags/uncertainties, gave opinionated judgment, landed action homework, gave minimum validation plan
